'''Alfred Leon Foster''' (1904-1994) was an [[American mathematician]].<ref name=BerkeleyObit>[http://texts.cdlib.org/view?docId=hb238nb0fs&doc.view=entire_text Alfred L. Foster, U. of California: In Memoriam, 1995]</ref> He was a professor at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], from 1934 until 1971.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www-history.mcs.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Foster.html|title=Alfred Leon Foster|publisher=MacTutor|access-date=28 January 2016}}</ref> In 1932, he was an Invited Speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] in Zürich.

In 1934, he accepted a regular position at [[University of California Berkeley|Berkeley]]. At that time, [[Griffith Evans]] was Head of the Mathematics Department and was charged by President Sproul with building a first-class mathematics center, which he did. Alfred Foster and [[Charles Morrey]] (the first department chairman after Evans' retirement) were Evans' first two appointments. Except for subsequent sabbatical leaves, spent most notably in [[University of Freiburg|Freiburg]] and [[University of Tübingen|Tübingen]], Foster served continuously at Berkeley until his retirement at the then-mandatory age of 67 in 1971.

Foster's Ph.D. dissertation and his first few papers were in [[mathematical logic]]. From this point, he soon focused on the related theory of [[Boolean algebras]] and [[Boolean rings]] and was thus led from logic to algebra. He extensively studied the role of [[Duality (mathematics)|duality]] in Boolean theory. Subsequently, he developed a theory of n-ality for certain rings, which played for [[Many-valued logic|n-valued logics]] the role of Boolean rings vis-a-vis Boolean algebras. The late [[Benjamin Abram Bernstein|Benjamin Bernstein]] of the Berkeley mathematics faculty was his collaborator in some of this research. This work culminated in his seminal paper "The Theory of Boolean-like Rings", appearing in 1946.<ref name=BerkeleyObit/>

Foster was married to Else Wagner;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://paw.princeton.edu/memorials/57/63/index.xml|title=Alfred Leon Foster *31|date=25 October 1995|publisher=Princeton Alumni Weekly|access-date=28 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160203143150/https://paw.princeton.edu/memorials/57/63/index.xml|archive-date=2016-02-03|url-status=dead}}</ref> their marriage produced four children and eight grandchildren.<ref name=BerkeleyObit/>
